headline: Open-Source System Turns Claude Code Into a Full Engineering Team
lede: Anthropic's coding agent, Claude Code, ships as a capable but essentially solo assistant. Everything Claude Code, an open-source repository published in January 2026 by San Francisco developer Affaan Mustafa, reframes the tool as a modular system of 28 specialized subagents, 116 skills, and roughly 60 slash commands—standing up a virtual engineering team inside a single terminal. The project won the Anthropic x Forum Ventures hackathon at Cerebral Valley in September 2025 before going public, and has since accumulated over 91,000 GitHub stars.
body:
**Claude Code**, released by Anthropic in early 2025, lets developers interact with a codebase through natural language in a terminal. By default, a single agent reads, writes, and runs code—competent but undifferentiated. Everything Claude Code inverts that model. Rather than one generalist, the system deploys 28 agents each tuned for a specific role: Python reviewer, TypeScript reviewer, database analyst, security auditor, and others. The result is closer to a pull-request queue staffed by specialists than a conversation with a single pair-programmer.

The building blocks are *skills*—116 reusable knowledge modules covering coding standards, test-driven development workflows, backend and frontend architecture patterns, and domain-specific playbooks for Django, Laravel, Spring Boot, and Go. Alongside these, the repo ships roughly 60 slash commands that replace ad hoc prompts with repeatable workflows: /plan, /code-review, /security-scan, /build-fix. *Hooks*—shell commands wired to session lifecycle events—let the system automatically load context at the start of a session and save progress at the end, giving the AI a form of persistent memory across projects.

Security receives dedicated treatment. A module called **AgentShield** adds an agent-level threat scanner, addressing a class of risk that most coding-assistant setups ignore: the possibility that AI agents themselves become attack surfaces through *prompt injection* (where malicious text in a repo or tool response hijacks the agent's instructions), unsafe tool calls, or unsanitized inputs from third-party sources. The repo's accompanying security guide covers sandboxing, sanitization, and known CVEs relevant to agentic workflows—an acknowledgment that systems with autonomous tool-calling permissions require their own threat model.

Mustafa had been refining the system privately since Claude Code's experimental rollout in February 2025, won the Anthropic hackathon in September 2025, and released the whole thing under the MIT license in January 2026. The architecture also extends beyond Claude Code: the repo documents support for Cursor, OpenAI Codex, and other coding agents, positioning it less as a Claude-specific plugin and more as a candidate standard for the emerging discipline of *agent harness* design—the art of configuring, constraining, and orchestrating AI agents in production engineering environments.

concepts.definition: The configuration and orchestration layer that governs how AI agents are instantiated, what tools they can call, what rules they must follow, and how they hand work off to one another. A harness is distinct from the underlying model; it shapes behavior without changing the weights.

Reusable knowledge modules—structured prompts and domain context—that prime an agent for a specific task. Rather than writing a new prompt each time, a developer loads a skill like 'django-tdd' and the agent inherits the relevant patterns, constraints, and vocabulary for that domain.

Shell commands configured to fire automatically in response to agent lifecycle events—session start, tool call, session end. They allow the system to load context, enforce policies, or save state without requiring the developer to issue explicit instructions each time.

An open standard from Anthropic that lets AI assistants connect to external tools, data sources, and services through a unified interface. An MCP server exposes capabilities—web search, database queries, file access—that the agent can call as structured tools rather than free-form text requests.

An attack where malicious text embedded in an external source—a repository README, a web page, a tool's response—causes an AI agent to override its instructions or take unintended actions. It is the agentic equivalent of SQL injection: the boundary between data and instructions collapses.

repos.summary: A fork or mirror of the Everything Claude Code system originally built by Affaan Mustafa, providing an agent harness for Claude Code and compatible coding agents. It bundles 28 specialized subagents, 116 skills, 60 slash commands, automated hooks, MCP server integrations, and the AgentShield security scanner under an MIT license. The original project won the Anthropic x Forum Ventures hackathon in September 2025 and was released publicly in January 2026.

fact_check: The tweet image shows '50K+ stars' in a static banner, while research sources published around the same period report over 91,000 stars approaching 100,000—suggesting the banner text was written at an earlier point and not updated as the count grew. This is a presentation artifact rather than a false claim. The tweet's figures of 28 agents, 116 skills, and 59 commands are consistent with sources, which cite 119 skills and roughly 60 commands; the small discrepancy likely reflects versioning between the screenshot and the sources.
